versions.name: The original release
versions.summary: The launch build: seven levels, two forms and the first level editor. Every version below started here.
versions.context: The first public build set the template: a square that jumps, a ship that flies, and a level editor that turns players into creators.
notes: Seven official levels, from Stereo Madness to Jumper.
Cube and ship forms across seven official levels.
A built-in level editor and online level sharing.
Released for iOS and Android on 13 August 2013.

arcade.name: Launch run
arcade.tagline: Seven levels, two forms, one place to start. Clear the line to log a time.

versions.name: Time Machine & mirror mode
versions.summary: The first major update added Time Machine and flipped the screen with the mirror portal. Players could also comment on and dislike user levels.
versions.context: Mirror mode was the headline mechanic, but comments and dislikes turned the level browser into a community.
notes: Time Machine added as the eighth official level.
The mirror portal flips the camera horizontally.
Level comments and dislikes added to the online browser.

arcade.name: Mirror run
arcade.tagline: The first update is a change of direction. Keep the cube moving and clear the line.

versions.name: Cycles & the ball
versions.summary: The ball form arrived, adding a gravity-swapping rhythm to the game, along with a new level and two cubes for the icon kit.
versions.context: The ball added a second rhythm: tap to swap gravity and keep the run alive.
notes: Cycles added as the ninth official level.
The ball form introduced gravity-flip controls.
Two new cube icons added to the icon kit.

arcade.name: Gravity run
arcade.tagline: Tap the ceiling, land on the floor, repeat. A one-button course for the ball era.

versions.name: xStep & blue orbs
versions.summary: Blue jump orbs and pads gave creators a new way to chain jumps mid-air. xStep showed off what the editor could do.
versions.context: Blue orbs and pads gave creators a way to chain jumps in mid-air instead of relying on the ground.
notes: xStep added as the tenth official level.
Blue jump orbs and blue pads added to the editor.
New decorations and effects for user levels.

arcade.name: Mid-air run
arcade.tagline: A course for chaining jumps. One button, no orbs, no excuses.

versions.name: Clutterfunk & size portals
versions.summary: Mini and big portals let players shrink or grow mid-level for the first time, and ship icons gained proper two-tone colouring.
versions.context: Size portals changed the scale of a level, letting one screen hold a tiny cube or a giant ship.
notes: Clutterfunk added as the eleventh official level.
Mini and big portals change the player's size mid-level.
Four new ship icons and two-tone ship colouring.

arcade.name: Scale run
arcade.tagline: A compact course built around close timing. Clear the line to log a time.

versions.name: Theory of Everything & the UFO
versions.summary: The UFO form introduced tap-to-flap flying, alongside magenta pads and rings. User levels could be rated Demon for the first time.
versions.context: The UFO brought tap-to-flap flight, and Demon difficulty gave the hardest user levels a label.
notes: Theory of Everything added as the twelfth official level.
The UFO form introduced tap-to-flap flight.
Magenta pads and rings added to the editor.
Demon difficulty added for user levels.

arcade.name: Flight run
arcade.tagline: The UFO era, translated into a one-button ground course. Keep the rhythm.

versions.name: Electroman Adventures & Clubstep
versions.summary: Secret coins were added to every level and Clubstep became the first official Demon. Map packs and destructible blocks rounded out the update.
versions.context: Secret coins and Clubstep gave completionists something to chase beyond the main path.
notes: Electroman Adventures and Clubstep added.
Three secret coins hidden in every official level.
Map packs collect user levels into ordered challenges.
Destructible blocks added to the editor.

arcade.name: Coin run
arcade.tagline: A longer course with less breathing room. Clear the line to log a time.

versions.name: Electrodynamix & speed changes
versions.summary: Speed portals brought slow, normal, fast and very fast gameplay, plus new backgrounds, a rainbow trail and glow effects.
versions.context: Speed portals let a single level shift pace, and the glow effects made fast sections readable.
notes: Electrodynamix added as the next official level.
Speed portals for slow, normal, fast and very fast sections.
New backgrounds and a rainbow trail.
Glow effects added to the editor.

arcade.name: Speed run
arcade.tagline: A faster course for the update that made speed a mechanic. Stay ahead of the line.

versions.name: Hexagon Force & dual mode
versions.summary: Dual portals put two icons on screen at once, while slopes changed how levels could be built. Hexagon Force tied it all together.
versions.context: Dual mode ran two icons at once; slopes made the editor feel less like a grid of blocks.
notes: Hexagon Force added as the next official level.
Dual portals put two player icons on screen at once.
Slopes added to the level editor.

arcade.name: Dual run
arcade.tagline: Two rhythms, one button. A course for the update that doubled the screen.

versions.name: Blast Processing & the wave
versions.summary: The wave form arrived with two new levels. Editor layers and a 20,000-object limit landed, and the game reached Steam on 22 December 2014.
versions.context: The wave added a precision flight pattern, editor layers cleaned up complex builds, and the game reached Steam.
notes: Blast Processing and Theory of Everything 2 added.
The wave form introduced precision flight controls.
Editor layers and a 20,000-object limit.
Geometry Dash released on Steam on 22 December 2014.
versions.forms: Cube, ship, ball, UFO, wave, dual

arcade.name: Wave run
arcade.tagline: The end of the 1.x era. A tighter course with a smaller margin for error.

versions.name: Geometrical Dominator & Deadlocked
versions.summary: The robot form landed with two levels, user coins and moving objects. Accounts gained friends, following and messaging, plus the first secret vault.
versions.context: The robot and user coins arrived together, alongside the first steps toward a proper account system.
notes: Geometrical Dominator and Deadlocked added.
The robot form introduced a new jump rhythm.
User coins and moving objects added to the editor.
Accounts gained friends, following and messaging.
The first secret vault opened.
versions.forms: Cube, ship, ball, UFO, wave, robot, dual

arcade.name: Robot run
arcade.tagline: A new decade, a new form. Clear the line to log a 2.0 time.

versions.name: Fingerdash & the spider
versions.summary: The spider form, dash orbs and custom rings arrived, alongside diamonds, the diamond shop and a round of editor improvements.
versions.context: The spider and dash orbs changed how players thought about momentum, while diamonds added a second currency.
notes: Fingerdash added as the next official level.
The spider form introduced a new movement pattern.
Dash orbs and custom rings added to the editor.
Diamonds, the diamond shop and editor improvements.
versions.forms: Cube, ship, ball, UFO, wave, robot, spider, dual

arcade.name: Dash run
arcade.tagline: A course built for quick decisions. The line is the only target.

versions.name: Dash, the swing & Editor 2.0
versions.summary: The biggest update yet: the swing form, Dash, 86 new editor triggers, free-camera controls, platformer mode and Lists. It landed on Steam on 19 December 2023 and on mobile the next day.
versions.context: Editor 2.0 was the real event: triggers, camera control, platformer mode and Lists turned the editor into a small engine.
notes: Dash added as the latest official level.
The swing form introduced a new take on gravity.
86 new editor triggers and free-camera controls.
Platformer mode and Lists added to the game.
Steam release on 19 December 2023; mobile on 20 December.
versions.forms: Cube, ship, ball, UFO, wave, robot, spider, swing, dual

arcade.name: Swing run
arcade.tagline: The latest era, tuned to the fastest course in the archive. Clear the line to log a time.

versions.label: Lite
versions.name: The free cut
versions.summary: The free cut of the game, with a rotating selection of main levels and its own unlocks.
versions.context: A free cut of the game with a rotating sample of main levels, built to let new players try before buying.
notes: Free edition with a rotating selection of main levels.
Separate save and unlock path from the paid game.
Released for mobile in 2013.

arcade.name: Lite run
arcade.tagline: A shorter course for the free edition. Same one-button rules, no purchase required.

versions.label: Meltdown
versions.name: Three levels, one soundtrack
versions.summary: Three levels — The Seven Seas, Viking Arena and Airborne Robots — with an F-777 soundtrack.
versions.context: A short, free-standing three-level pack with its own soundtrack and a darker visual theme.
facts: The Seven Seas, Viking Arena, Airborne Robots
notes: Three levels: The Seven Seas, Viking Arena and Airborne Robots.
Original soundtrack by F-777.
Standalone release on 19 December 2015.
versions.levels: The Seven Seas, Viking Arena, Airborne Robots

arcade.name: Meltdown run
arcade.tagline: A darker, faster course for the three-level spin-off. Clear the line to log a time.

versions.label: World
versions.name: Ten levels, two worlds
versions.summary: Ten short levels across two worlds, plus daily levels and an early look at 2.1 features.
versions.context: Ten bite-sized levels split across two worlds, with daily challenges and an early look at 2.1.
notes: Ten short levels across two worlds.
Daily levels added as a recurring challenge.
Early access to mechanics that would reach 2.1.
Released on 21 December 2016.
versions.levels: Ten short levels across two worlds
versions.forms: Cube, ship, ball, UFO, wave, robot

arcade.name: World run
arcade.tagline: A quick tour through the World era. One button, one line, one time to beat.

versions.label: SubZero
versions.name: A three-level teaser
versions.summary: Press Start, Nock Em and Power Trip — a three-level teaser for the mechanics of 2.2.
versions.context: A three-level teaser that put some of 2.2's ideas in players' hands a few years early.
facts: Press Start, Nock Em, Power Trip
notes: Three levels: Press Start, Nock Em and Power Trip.
A teaser for mechanics that would define 2.2.
Released on 21 December 2017.
